reason: The goal is to supply fuel, and this is the only available action.
expectation: I expect the sugar to supply the muscle fibers with fuel; oxygen may be added later.

effect: The fibers now process sugar, and the diagram suggests another stage involving mitochondria. Adding oxygen is the only offered combination.
reaction: The separate arrows make me curious about how oxygen contributes to ATP production.
reason: Oxygen is the remaining supply named in the goal, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect oxygen to help the fibers use the processed fuel for continued cellular work, though I am unsure how the result will explain it.

effect: Oxygen and fuel support ATP production, and the new goal shifts attention to gathering the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The ATP-to-ADP cycle helps connect energy supply to muscle work, though the diagram introduces ADP without explaining it.
reason: Wrapping the fibers seems like a first step toward collecting their pulls, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the wrapping to group the fibers so their pulls can be transmitted together.

effect: The wrapping gathered the muscle cells into bundles, and their exposed ends suggest they are ready for tendons.
reaction: The shared sleeve makes the grouping clear, though the result is fairly predictable.
reason: Front tendons seem like a practical way to attach the bundles and transmit their pull; I have no clear reason to prefer them over rear tendons.
expectation: I expect the front tendons to attach to the muscle bundles, forming one muscle group.

alternatives.reason: Rear tendons also appear suitable, but I chose to start with the front.

effect: The front tendons produced bending muscles, and the result explains that tendons transmit a pull to an attachment. The remaining combination can make the other muscle group.
reaction: The link between tendons and moving a joint is clear, and I am curious how the two groups will work together.
reason: Rear tendons are the only offered combination and should complete the second muscle group.
expectation: I expect the rear tendons and bundles to form a second muscle group, perhaps one that straightens a joint.

effect: The rear tendons formed straightening muscles, completing the second muscle group and the chapter’s goals.
reaction: The result matched my expectation, though I would have liked to see how the two groups move a joint.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was most worthwhile because the result connected fuel and oxygen to ATP and muscle work. ADP appeared without an explanation, though.

leastWorthwhile.text: Wrapping the fibers was predictable, and the result added little beyond showing them grouped in a sleeve.

surprise.text: The sugar-processing result showed separate paths toward ATP and the mitochondrion, which made me curious about the next stage.

arbitrary.text: Choosing front before rear tendons felt arbitrary: both were offered and I had no clear reason to prefer either.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the bending and straightening muscles attach to bones and work together at a joint.
